title: Nepal Beat UAE to Win ACC Premier Cup and Book Asia Cup 2027 Spot
excerpt: Aasif Sheikh's century and Gulsan Jha's late assault powered Nepal to 313, before Karan KC and Lalit Rajbanshi derailed a UAE chase anchored by Rahul Chopra's unbeaten hundred at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur.
body:
• Nepal beat the UAE by 44 runs in the final of the ACC Men's Premier Cup 2026 at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur on September 12, sealing qualification for the Asia Cup 2027 — only their second appearance at the continental championship.
  • Aasif Sheikh's 102 off 106 balls anchored Nepal's 313/9, with a late assault from Gulsan Jha (52 off 38) lifting them past 300; Ibrar Ahmad was the UAE's standout bowler with 4/62.
  • Chasing 314, the UAE collapsed from 45/0 to 119/5 before Rahul Chopra's unbeaten 100 and Sohaib Khan's 52 revived hopes; Nepal bowled them out for 269 in 49.1 overs.
  • The UAE, led by captain Harpreet Singh Bhatia and powered by several players of Indian origin, fell short despite a spirited fightback, while Nepal captain Sandeep Lamichhane was named Player of the Series for his 17 wickets.

The Final in Kuala Lumpur

Nepal are heading back to the Asia Cup. On Saturday, September 12, they brushed aside the United Arab Emirates by 44 runs in the final of the ACC Men's Premier Cup 2026 at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur, winning the title and booking their place at the Asia Cup 2027 — only their second appearance at Asia's top cricketing championship after the 2023 edition.

Having won the toss and opted to bat, Nepal posted 313/9 in their 50 overs — their highest-ever ODI total against the UAE and their third-highest overall — before bowling out the Emiratis for 269 in 49.1 overs.

Sheikh's Century Sets the Platform

Wicketkeeper-batter Aasif Sheikh was named Player of the Match for a match-defining hundred. His 102 came off 106 balls with eight fours and four sixes, and more than half his runs came in boundaries as he ensured Nepal never lost momentum through the middle overs.

Openers Arjun Kumal (43 off 63) and Sheikh put on a solid 97-run stand in 21 overs, immediately putting the UAE on the back foot. UAE captain Harpreet Singh Bhatia finally manufactured a run-out opportunity off the last ball of the 21st over to remove Kumal, and Ishan Pandey fell soon after for 13. But former captain Rohit Paudel (40 off 44) added 68 for the third wicket with Sheikh to steady the innings before Haider Ali removed the centurion in the 36th over.

Gulsan Jha then provided the late-innings burst that pushed Nepal past 300, smashing 52 off 38 balls with three fours and four sixes. Basir Ahamad's four-ball 15 not out lifted the total to a commanding 313. Ibrar Ahmad was the UAE's standout bowler with figures of 4/62 from eight overs.

Chopra's Lone Resistance

The UAE's chase of 314 started brightly, with openers Tanish Suri and Adeeb Usmani adding 45 in five overs. But the innings collapsed dramatically, slipping from 45/0 to 119/5 as Nepal's attack squeezed the middle order.

Sohaib Khan (52 off 57) and Rahul Chopra then mounted a spirited fightback, stitching an 87-run stand for the sixth wicket to revive Emirati hopes. But Sohaib's dismissal in the 39th over effectively ended the challenge, leaving Chopra to battle alone. He remained unbeaten on 100 off 105 balls — a fighting century with three fours and four sixes — but lacked the support to finish the job, and the tail folded for 269.

Karan KC (3/49) and Lalit Rajbanshi (2/43) were Nepal's key performers with the ball, while Sandeep Lamichhane, Dipendra Singh Airee, Rohit Paudel, Gulsan Jha, and Basir Ahamad each chipped in with a wicket to dismantle the UAE lineup. Captain Lamichhane's 17 wickets across the tournament earned him the Player of the Series award.

Diaspora Angle

The final had a distinctly diaspora flavour. The UAE side was stacked with players of Indian origin — captain Harpreet Singh Bhatia, centurion Rahul Chopra, Tanish Suri, Akshdeep Nath, and Adeeb Usmani all featured — a reminder of how deeply the Indian diaspora powers associate-nation cricket in the Gulf. That an Indian-origin batter produced the innings of the match for the UAE, even in defeat, is a story in itself for NRI fans who follow the Emirates' cricketing rise.

What's Next

Nepal now joins Asia's top cricketing nations at the Asia Cup 2027, where they will test themselves against full-member opposition. For the UAE, the runners-up finish closes a strong campaign — they were also the previous edition's winners — but leaves them watching the continental showpiece from home. The 44-run margin flattered the chase; Nepal were the better side on the day, and their young core, built around Paudel, Sheikh, and Lamichhane, has a full season of one-day cricket ahead to prepare.
